content.body:
Fast and low profile, the A15 (Crusader II) was an evolution of the A13 with slightly better armor. Unfortunately, it still bore the 2pdr. cannon which was quickly becoming obsolescent against up-armored Pz.IIIHs and Pz.IVGs.
The initial productions of the Crusader II also included another crewman serving a bow-mounted machinegun in sub turret at the left front; this was found to be cramped, poorly ventilated, and nearly impossible to escape in an emergency and so was generally removed.
Control Variations: Driver spawns in with view slit armor in place, can zoom on open viewslit (numpad . or Del key). Key O opens bigger view window, driver can also zoom on this view (numpad . or Del key). AP ammunition only and no range adjustment or gradation available through gunsight.
Functionally almost identical to the A13, the A15 is a good tank with a gun capable of killing most medium tanks. The green color and QF.2pdr gun make it excellent from ambush, although the characteristically weak British optics somewhat negate the range advantage of the 2pdr. By the time the A15 is in the field, some of the German tanks are impervious to the 2pdr form the front; you will need to be more circumspect and look for side or rear-aspect shots to succeed. Drive it like an armored car pay close attention to your situation and don't stand and fight anything. Don't be afraid to stop and look around, as long as you're in cover; the green coloring will hide you from cursory examination.
As with the A13, you should fear air attack, your roof/deck armor can be penetrated even by aircraft machineguns. If you are immobilized by enemy fire (as long as you're not burning with a big black cloud of smoke), don't despawn. The camouflage paint is again useful in deceiving your opponents.
content.brief: TYPE: Medium AFV ARMAMENT: 40mm Main Gun (QF.2pdr) 1 x .303 inch MG WEIGHT: 19272 kg SPEED.(road): 48 km/h
